name: Azul

setup.text: Arrange the Factory displays in a circle in the middle of the table.
Put all 100 tiles (20 of each colour) in the bag.
Return unused boards, markers and displays to the box.
Take a player board and turn it to the coloured wall side. Everyone must use the same side.
Put your scoring marker on 0 of your score track.
Whoever most recently visited Portugal takes the starting player marker and fills each Factory display with 4 tiles drawn from the bag.

turn.summary: Each round has three phases: Factory offer, Wall-tiling, then preparing the next round. During the Factory offer you take tiles one of two ways.
steps: Take all tiles of one colour from one Factory display and push the rest of that display into the centre, or take all tiles of one colour from the centre.
The first player to take from the centre in a round also takes the starting player marker and puts it on their floor line.
Add the tiles to one pattern line, filling right to left. A line holds one colour only. Tiles that don't fit go to your floor line.
When the displays and centre are empty, everyone tiles: move the rightmost tile of each full pattern line to the wall and score it, then clear those lines.

round_end: Lose the points printed above each tile in your floor line, then clear it. Your score cannot drop below 0.
The player with the starting player marker refills every display with 4 tiles. If the bag is empty, refill it from the box lid.
end: The game ends after the Wall-tiling phase in which at least one player has completed a horizontal row of 5 tiles on their wall.

scoring.text: A tile placed with nothing next to it scores 1 point.
Otherwise count the tiles linked to it in its row, including itself, and score that many; then do the same for its column.
End of game: 2 points for each complete horizontal row, 7 for each complete vertical column, 10 for each colour you have placed all 5 tiles of.

tiebreak: More complete horizontal rows; if still tied, the win is shared.

missed.text: You cannot put a colour in a pattern line if that row of your wall already has that colour.
The starting player marker counts as a tile in your floor line and costs points.
If your floor line is full, further dropped tiles go to the box lid with no extra penalty.
You may choose to put tiles you take straight onto your floor line.
